about: #4628: each surviving det-port mutant stated `equivalent` or `unreachable`, with the Java change and why it cannot alter observable behaviour; proposed in a PR, reviewed by the owner. A run that kills a stated mutant fails (the claim was wrong). Ids are mutation.py's; before / after are the Java line.

verdicts.equivalent: the change cannot alter anything the program shows (output, screen, files, COMMAREA, abend)
verdicts.unreachable: no input of the program reaches the changed code
verdicts.harness-gap: the change alters behaviour the proof runs but does not compare (open: the harness must)
verdicts.case-gap: an input the case lacks would kill it (open: strengthen the case)

the scan over outer PERFORMs iterates only when a paragraph that is not its range's last returns inside a nested PERFORM; COADM01C's PERFORMs each name one paragraph (from == thru), MAIN-PARA (runTask's 0-7) always ends in RETURN / XCTL, and the GO TO into PGMIDERR-ERR-PARA ends in its RETURN, so the scan never iterates
MOVE SPACES TO WS-MESSAGE at MAIN-PARA's start: every task starts from initialState, where WS-MESSAGE is already spaces (WS-VARIABLES' image), and nothing writes it before this statement

MAIN-PARA's MOVE SPACES TO ERRMSGO is a dead store: every path that sends the map goes through SEND-MENU-SCREEN, whose first act (COADM01C line 180) is MOVE WS-MESSAGE TO ERRMSGO, and the other paths XCTL or RETURN without sending.

The final RETURN TRANSID(CA00) re-enters COADM01C itself, and the next task is the only reader of the COMMAREA length (its EIBCALEN). COADM01C uses EIBCALEN twice: IF EIBCALEN = 0 (line 86), false at 160 and at 161; and MOVE DFHCOMMAREA(1:EIBCALEN) TO CARDDEMO-COMMAREA (line 90), a 160-byte target, so the extra byte of 161 is truncated. DFHCOMMAREA is read nowhere else. The proof does not compare the length argument (a chained next-task run is not modelled), so this is stated from the program's own reads, proposed for owner review.

survivors.reason: The scan loop stops at WS-IDX = 1 in the original; the mutant stops at WS-IDX = 2 (the start). The next statement moves OPTIONI(1:WS-IDX) into WS-OPTION-X, a PIC X(2), which space-pads: OPTIONI(1:1) padded and OPTIONI(1:2) are the same two bytes whenever byte 2 is a space, the only case the loop body runs.

Stepping WS-IDX up instead of down: with OPTIONI byte 2 blank the mutant reads past OPTIONI into ERRMSGL (a halfword whose high byte is low-values, not a space), so the loop stops at index 3; OPTIONI(1:3) moved into the PIC X(2) WS-OPTION-X truncates to the same two bytes the original gets.
